panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Real patient posterior-anterior chest radiograph in female with X-linked agammaglobulinemia showing left lower lobe opacity, but opacity/bronchiectasis/sinus disease are not in allowed vocabulary which only contains absent/small tonsils and absent cervical lymph nodes; per rule 6 no vocabulary finding can be named so panel excluded. b: Real patient sagittal chest CT showing cylindrical bronchiectasis in lingula and left lower lobe in X-linked agammaglobulinemia, but this manifestation is not in allowed vocabulary; no absent tonsils/lymph nodes visible, so excluded. c: Real patient head CT showing bilateral mucosal thickening of maxillary sinuses in X-linked agammaglobulinemia, but sinus thickening is not in allowed vocabulary; no vocabulary finding can be named so excluded.

in_text_mentions: This patient received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) replacement (0.5 g/kg every 4 weeks) and, there times per week oral azithromycin prophylaxis, 10 mg/kg orally for frequent pulmonary exacerbations. There was some reduction of her productive cough, and her rhinosinusitis has also improved after six months of therapy. Her IgG levels were normal with replacement therapy (Fig. 1).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Chest CT of the patient in a case report titled 'Fatal X-linked agammaglobulinemia complicated by septic shock'; the caption and text identify patchy pulmonary high-density shadows in this XLA patient. No vocabulary finding_key (ENT/tonsil items) applies, so findings are recorded as proposed terms. Pulmonary infection is a hallmark complication of XLA but does not by itself prove disease specificity, hence moderate confidence. B: Direct visualization of right lower lobe consolidation matching the in-text description of the XLA patient's chest CT; disease attribution rests on the case-report title and caption context, no ENT-vocabulary finding is present. C: Panel shows the described right lower-lobe involvement and pleural effusion in the XLA patient; attribution from article title plus captioned manifestation, findings recorded as proposed terms outside the ENT-only vocabulary. D: Consolidation and effusion at the right base directly...
panels.attribution_text: Wu et al. Fatal X-linked agammaglobulinemia complicated by septic shock: a case report and comprehensive review of novel BTK mutations.. Frontiers in immunology 2025. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2025.1645337. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: Chest CT revealed patchy high-density shadows in the left lower lobe and right lung, with significant involvement of the right lower lobe and a small amount of right pleural effusion ( Figure 1 ). Bedside thoracic ultrasound confirmed bilateral pleural effusion. Cardiac ultrasound indicated tachycardia, while abdominal, lower limb, and urinary tract ultrasounds showed no abnormalities.
